title: The Third Trap
text: The airship is parked in the grasslands just outside the castle town. I remember that. They’re luring us onto the ship to trap us, just like last time.
“Ah, the national representatives, please board this airship, and the Heroes, please board that one over there.”
“Why is that?”
The Queen asks the Faubrey soldier leading the way. The Faubrey soldier’s face twitches as if surprised by the question.
“The request is that while the Heroes are in the meeting, the representatives from each nation plan their upcoming strategy in a separate room.”
“Wouldn’t it be better if the Heroes were present for that?”
“Of course, they’ll be able to talk while they’re moving. The Whip Hero has suggested that there are matters and discussions that can only be conveyed between Heroes themselves.”

He’s implying that the Heroes would feel too nervous to speak freely in front of royalty and representatives, but since they understand each other’s minds, it’s easier for them to coordinate. So he’s saying it’s better to let the Heroes stay together. But… from our perspective, knowing how Takt acts, we can see right through this—it’s clearly a trap. I hope the Heroes can actually relax this way.
“…Understood. Well then, Mr. Iwatani, Mr. Kitamura. We’ll leave it to you.”
“Please, for the sake of the world, board the ship quickly… Just a moment.”
Just as my father and I were about to board the ship we’d been escorted to with our companions, a soldier called out to my father-in-law’s Finacée, who was part of his entourage.
“If I’m not mistaken, you must be Princess Melty Melromarc of this country. Please board the ship with the Queen.”
“I refuse.”
My finacée clings to the hem of my Father’s cloak and refuses. But the soldier won’t back down.
“Please, I implore you.”
“She’s part of my party, you know?”
My Father says, furrowing his brow in annoyance.
“I understand that, as a Hero, you’ve established friendly ties with the royal family. However, we’ve received orders that Heroes should keep their distance from those in power to relax, so please…”

He won’t back down an inch. This is it, isn’t it? Since Melromarc, Siltvelt, and Takt himself haven’t quite made up their minds to go to war, they’re trying to ward off the watchful eyes of the royal family and others to avoid arousing suspicion as much as possible. After all, there’s a risk if they can’t cover it up properly.

Last time, they probably had a plan to cover it up. But now, especially since the Queen and her Finacée are always nearby, even if they try to pull a fast one with a body double or Magic, their own people probably wouldn’t be fooled.
“Melty, let’s get ready so we don’t cause too much trouble for Lord Iwatani.”
“But…”
The Queen beckons.
“In exchange, I’d like you to send one of Lord Iwatani’s companions—one of Melty’s friends—to serve as our escort.”
“That’s right. Melty and her friends might actually be better for Sakura-chan.”

Father is subtly instructing Sakura-chan to keep her safe. I see—the Queen has thought this through. Indeed, there’s no guarantee they won’t harm not only us but also the people of Melromarc and Siltvelt. In that case, it’d be best to have someone assigned as a bodyguard.
“Huh? Is Naofumi going to be okay?”
“He’ll be fine! Gaelion will protect Naofumi!”
“Boo!”
When her Rival spoke up, Sakura-chan objected. “You just stay out of this,” she seemed to say.
“Gaelion, just be quiet. Wyndia, please look after Gaelion.”
“Okay.”
“Sakura-chan… I’m counting on you to look after Melty-chan and everyone else.”
My father earnestly entrusted Sakura-chan with this task. Perhaps sensing his intention, Sakura-chan nodded.
“Got it!”
With Sakura-chan present, my Finacée let go of my father’s hand and headed toward the Queen.
“Well then, I’ll leave it to you.”
“Yes.”
Despite being in a hurry, their planning is quite evident. If this were really just a discussion, it would be the kind of thing you’d just laugh off. We’re clattering up the stairs.
“Whoops.”

Just as we started climbing, we heard a sound like the Queen was about to fall. That was… on purpose, wasn’t it? She’s probably trying to buy as much time as possible to make sure there are no problems. Meanwhile, the elderly Gemu is walking slowly with a suspicious gait, pretending to be a senile old man.
So, we entered the airship. Keel is looking around excitedly.
“It looks like the ship we took when we went to Cal Mira Island.”
“Well, it’s an airship. Since it has ‘ship’ in the name, I guess there are some similarities.”
“But the rooms and stuff probably look different.”
“Hmm… I guess there are a lot of differences? Actually, this is my first time on an airship, too.”
“Naofumi, do you want to take a trip through the sky? Gaelion will show you around.”
“Hmm… well, riding on Gaelion-chan’s back does sound fun, though.”
“Gaelion will never forget Naofumi’s words for the rest of her life!”
“What!?”

And so on—we’re making our way through the airship in a carefree sort of mood. The atmosphere is exactly the same as last time. It’d be fine if Takt were prioritizing his mission to save the world, but my Ki tells me otherwise.

So, I guess I’ll start my incantation now so I can be ready for battle as soon as possible? We pass through a generously sized hallway and are led to what looks like an observation deck. There, as always, Takt is sitting back arrogantly with a line of pigs lined up against the wall.
“You’re finally here.”
Seriously… Is this the only strategy this guy has? I’m so dumbfounded I can’t even speak.
“Um… I was invited here, but we’re having a strategy meeting, right?”
My Father must have confirmed his suspicions too, because he’s stepping up his guard. Keel, the Assistant, the Rival, and Yuki-chan and the others all go on high alert.
“Huh? Hahaha! Looks like the Four Holy Ones are a bunch of complete dreamers!”
Takt has stood up from his chair and is clasping his hands behind his back. He’s definitely planning to show his claws.
“You Four Holy Heroes who broke the seals on the Four Sealed Spirits! You’re all just as guilty! I’ll save the world myself, so die!”
And with that, Takt is about to unleash his one-trick-pony Skills. But before that, I quickly issued a certain… command.
“The Love Hunter commands: Vassal Weapons. Answer The Love Hunter’s call, break free from the shackles of foolish power, and awaken!”
The claw in Takt’s hand glows.
“—I hereby strip you of your status as a Servant!”
One, two, three, four… Oh, it must be a matter of timing, but there’s one more than last time.
“W-what!? What’s going on! Guh… My power is draining away! W-what the hell did you do!”

The Seven Star Weapons slip from Takt’s hands and float around us. I haven’t given the order yet. They’d probably rush out immediately even if I stayed silent, but first, let’s negotiate. All things considered, this airship’s maneuverability isn’t something to be taken lightly, and while they might be slightly inferior, these guys aren’t entirely without potential as immediate combat forces.
“Hahaha, it went exactly as I expected. Living in a fantasy world? That’s more like it.”
“What!?”
“Too bad. If you’d honestly wanted to save the world, things wouldn’t have turned out this way. To get you to listen to what I have to say, I’ve taken away your confidence.”

If you’re foolish enough to try to trap us, I’ll strip you of your Seven Star Weapons and use them as leverage to force you to promise to defeat the Phoenix and the Spirit Tortoise. It’s a punishment for setting the trap—a way to make you reflect on your actions.
